entrypoints.summary: The Swift utility tk_dataFromHexString accepts a caller-provided hexadecimal string and recursively strips an optional 0x prefix before decoding.

affected_components.role: Hexadecimal string-to-Data conversion routine containing the odd-length pairwise extraction behavior.

causal_paths.kind: odd-length hex input to wrong decoded Data

negative_controls: The report's even-length control 0x1234 is parsed as <1234>.
The expected padded representation for 0x123 is <0123>.
observability.positive_marker: The vulnerable conversion is reported as <1203> for 0x123.

preconditions: A caller reaches tk_dataFromHexString with a hexadecimal representation that has odd length after optional 0x-prefix removal.

trigger_steps.summary: Invoke the decoder with 0x123; after prefix removal, the odd-length string is processed in two-character strides.

capabilities.concept: noncanonical hexadecimal decoding to corrupted bytes

mitigations.concept: whole-string hexadecimal padding before byte extraction

relation_candidates.dst: noncanonical hexadecimal decoding to corrupted bytes
relation_candidates.rationale: Without full padding, the pairwise decoder processes an unmatched final nibble with the following C-string terminator and produces a wrong byte sequence.
The report demonstrates that 0x123 yields <1203> instead of expected <0123>.
relation_candidates.src: noncanonical hexadecimal decoding to corrupted bytes

relation_candidates.dst: whole-string hexadecimal padding before byte extraction
relation_candidates.rationale: Cure53 recommends fully padding the hex string before extracting single bytes, and reports an improved fixed algorithm verified by Cure53.
relation_candidates.src: noncanonical hexadecimal decoding to corrupted bytes

impact.affected_asset: Binary Data returned by tk_dataFromHexString; no security-sensitive downstream asset or wallet action is established.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause the utility to return a byte value different from the supplied odd-length hexadecimal value's expected padded representation.

causal_trace.summary: A caller supplies an odd-length hexadecimal representation after any optional 0x prefix is removed, such as 123.
The decoder does not ensure that the complete hexadecimal string is padded to an even number of nibbles before extracting bytes, so the text representation lacks canonical byte alignment.

The two-character stride copies chars[i] and chars[i + 1] into byteChars and calls strtoul for every iteration; on the unmatched final nibble, null termination avoids an immediate error but yields an incorrectly assembled byte.
The demonstrated odd-length input 0x123 decodes as bytes represented by 1203 rather than the expected 0123, passing a different binary value to downstream consumers.

failure.operation: Pairwise conversion of an odd-length hex string through byteChars and strtoul

primary_invariant.statement: A hexadecimal string must be fully padded to an even nibble count before pairwise byte extraction, so each textual value maps to its intended byte representation.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The implementation iterates in two-character units without first padding an odd-length input; its final extraction reads the unmatched nibble together with C-string termination.

raw_refs.role: canonical audit report, affected code, PoC, and fix note

quality.review_notes: The report supplies the affected function, a deterministic expected-versus-actual vector, a remediation recommendation, and a Cure53-verified fix statement. It does not identify an upstream patch revision or replacement code, show an executable test run, establish an external attacker boundary, or trace corrupted output into signing, transactions, authorization, keys, or another wallet-sensitive operation.

remediation.invariant_restored: The full hexadecimal representation is padded before bytes are extracted, ensuring that pairwise decoding preserves the expected canonical byte value.

affected_versions_or_commits.value: imToken wallet library assessed by Cure53 in 2018; no vulnerable upstream source revision is identified in the report

oracle.expected_negative: For an odd-length value, 0x123 must decode to <0123>, not the reported vulnerable result <1203>.
oracle.expected_positive: The report's correctly aligned control 0x1234 parses as <1234>.
